target.title: fix(qqbot): guard mentionPatterns against ReDoS via compileSafeRegex
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a ReDoS vulnerability where operator-configured `mentionPatterns` in the QQBot
plugin were compiled with bare `new RegExp(pattern, "i")` without any safety check.
A pattern containing nested repetition such as `(a+)+$` compiles successfully but
causes catastrophic backtracking when matched against attacker-controlled message
content, pushing CPU to 100% and making the gateway unresponsive.

Attack chain: set `mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"]` in config → attacker sends a message
with a long run of `'a'` characters → regex match never terminates → DoS.

The same class of bug was previously fixed in MCP glob patterns (#100330).
`compileSafeRegex` from `src/security/safe-regex.ts` is already exposed through
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/security-runtime` for exactly this use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `new RegExp(pattern, "i")` with `compileSafeRegex(pattern, "i")`. The helper
rejects patterns with nested repetition and returns `null` for both unsafe and invalid
patterns, so the loop simply skips them — same observable behavior as before for valid
safe patterns, silent rejection for dangerous ones.

## User Impact

**Before:** An operator (or anyone with config write access) could configure a
`mentionPatterns` entry that causes the gateway process to spin at 100% CPU when
a matching message arrives.

**After:** Patterns with nested repetition are rejected at match time and skipped.
Safe patterns continue to work normally.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/qqbot-mention-redos`  
Base: `upstream/main`  
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ detectWasMentioned > rejects ReDoS patterns via compileSafeRegex guard 0ms
 ✓ detectWasMentioned > still matches safe patterns after a rejected unsafe one 0ms
 ✓ detectWasMentioned > ignores invalid regex patterns gracefully 0ms
 ... (21 more)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
   Duration  1.60s
```

`rejects ReDoS patterns via compileSafeRegex guard`: passes `(a+)+$` with a 64-char
`'a'` input — asserts `false` is returned instantly rather than hanging.

`still matches safe patterns after a rejected unsafe one`: confirms the unsafe pattern
is skipped and the next safe pattern still matches.

### Diff summary

```
extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.ts      | +4 / -5  (import + replace)
extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.test.ts | +20      (2 new regression cases)
```

What was not tested: live QQBot message delivery with a real QQ group.
Crabbox/Testbox remote CI was not run at submission time.

## Real behavior proof

The timing probe exercised the production `detectWasMentioned` path directly against the
`compileSafeRegex` guard with the attack pattern `(a+)+$`. Node v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64.

**Before (raw `new RegExp` — catastrophic backtracking on non-matching input):**

```
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(20)+"b") →  65.5 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(24)+"b") → 156.9 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(26)+"b") → 640.7 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(28)+"b") → 2522.4 ms  (2.5 s — gateway would stall)
```

Each +2 characters roughly 4× the time (exponential growth). At 64 characters the gateway
process would be unresponsive for minutes.

**After (`compileSafeRegex` guard — constant-time rejection):**

```
compileSafeRegex("(a+)+$", "i") → null (rejected before RegExp construction)
detectWasMentioned({ content: "a".repeat(24)+"b", mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"] }) → false (0.065 ms)
detectWasMentioned({ content: "a".repeat(28)+"b", mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"] }) → false (0.003 ms)
```

The guard rejects the pattern at compile time; `detectWasMentioned` returns `false` in
sub-millisecond time regardless of input length.

**Safe pattern still matches after a rejected unsafe one:**

```
detectWasMentioned({
  content: "hello @bot",
  mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$", "@bot"],
}) → true (0.130 ms)
```

The unsafe entry is skipped; the next safe pattern matches normally.

**Production test suite (24/24):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ detectWasMentioned > rejects ReDoS patterns via compileSafeRegex guard  0ms
 ✓ detectWasMentioned > still matches safe patterns after a rejected unsafe one  0ms
 ✓ detectWasMentioned > ignores invalid regex patterns gracefully  0ms
 ... (21 more)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
   Duration  370ms
```

Live QQ platform traffic and a real QQ group were not used. The vulnerability was
reproduced via direct timing of the raw `RegExp` path; the fix was verified through the
production `detectWasMentioned` function and the full focused test suite.

Related: #100330 (MCP glob ReDoS — same fix pattern)

target.title: fix(ios): make Talk audio lifecycle-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelled or timed-out iOS push-to-talk work could remain queued and later acquire the microphone. Related asynchronous owners—including continuous Talk, realtime relay, Voice Wake, screen/camera audio, Gateway requests, speech playback, and restored session routing—could also outlive the app state, Gateway route, or chat session that created them.

Those races could restart stale capture, deliver a reply into a replacement session, let old cleanup stop a newer owner, or admit Talk before a cold-start routing identity finished restoring.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only push-to-talk capture preparation is serialized. Stop and cancel bypass that queue, while capture IDs, command epochs, and a finishing owner keep the microphone lease through transcript, chat, history, and speech completion.

App foreground state and explicit audio leases now gate every microphone owner. Talk, Voice Wake, realtime relay, ReplayKit capture, Gateway requests, speech tasks, and recognition callbacks use lifecycle generations or route leases so suspended work cannot mutate replacement state. Same-route reconnects preserve and await the pending SQLite routing restore; target switches cancel it and canceled loads cannot apply after suspension.

No Gateway protocol or public configuration surface changes.

## User Impact

Stopping, canceling, backgrounding, changing sessions, reconnecting, or replacing a Gateway can no longer let stale iOS voice work reopen the microphone, play an old reply, or affect the next session. Continuous Talk resumes only from its current owner, Voice Wake suppression follows the real audio owner, and camera/screen microphone capture remains single-owner and cancellation-safe.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `f19f6bb9c0b16d45faccb985477762e5b0306489`.
- Deterministic regressions cover queued and active PTT cancellation, finalizer ownership, session and route replacement, background admission, Voice Wake generations, realtime relay stop races, ReplayKit single-flight cleanup, Gateway cancellation, and routing hydration across reconnect/target switch.
- All 22 changed Swift files parse in DEBUG and Release modes; scoped SwiftFormat reports 0 files requiring formatting.
- Native i18n check passes with 2,916 entries; every unchanged localization identity retains its prior stable ID.
- `git diff --check` and the fresh whole-branch autoreview pass.
- Exact-head public CI and iOS Periphery results will be linked in the pre-land proof comment.
- Hardware gap: no physical iPhone is attached to this host, so microphone/privacy-indicator timing has deterministic lifecycle coverage and exact public CI, but no physical-device run.

target.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users interacting with agents through external chats such as WhatsApp could see automatic runtime notices when model fallback, usage limits, compaction, backend failures, heartbeat checks, ACP status, plugin-binding failures, or tool/progress warnings happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `messages.operationalReplies` so operators can control automatic operational notices separately from normal assistant replies. The policy supports `always`, `silent`, `once`, and `redirect`; `redirect` writes notices to an operator session through `redirectSessionKey`, and `sendPolicy: deny` still wins.

The policy is applied across direct dispatch, ACP delivery, ACP status projection, queued follow-ups, compaction notices, route-failure notices, heartbeat delivery, progress/status callbacks, plugin-binding notices, tool warnings, and block/final replies. Normal message-tool replies, authorized command replies, before-run block replies, and background ACP child suppression keep their existing behavior.

The branch was rebased during follow-up, and the unrelated WhatsApp shrinkwrap delta was removed from the PR. The `once` policy now records delivered notice fingerprints on the source session, so duplicate suppression survives process restarts instead of relying only on an in-memory set.

## User Impact

Operators can keep fallback, usage-limit, backend-error, compaction, heartbeat, status, ACP, follow-up, plugin-binding, and tool-warning notices out of external chats while still preserving logs or redirecting those notices to an operator-owned session. Existing configs keep current behavior because the default policy is `always`.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof: WhatsApp-like Source Chat

Earlier redacted terminal proof on this branch used the actual `applyOperationalReplyPolicy` helper, a real temp `sessions.json`, and a source context shaped like an external WhatsApp direct chat:

- source channel: `whatsapp`
- source session: `agent:main:whatsapp:direct:redacted-user`
- payload: `isError: true`, `isFallbackNotice: true`, text `model fallback failed; usage limit reached`

Observed output:

```text
silent: shouldDeliverToSourceChat=false, intentionalSilence=true, externalSends=0, opsTranscriptBytes=0
redirect: shouldDeliverToSourceChat=false, redirected=true, externalSends=0, opsTranscriptHasSourceSession=true, opsTranscriptHasSourceChannel=true, opsTranscriptHasNoticeText=true
redirect transcript excerpt: sourceSessionKey: agent:main:whatsapp:direct:redacted-user | sourceChannel: whatsapp | kind: error
```

This proves the affected external-source path does not deliver the operational fallback/error notice back to the source chat under `silent`, and under `redirect` it keeps source chat sends at zero while writing the notice, source session, source channel, and notice kind into the configured operator session transcript.

### Local Validation

Latest follow-up validation after rebasing on current `origin/main` and pushing `0c11afd128c71cd22d29cf9e7881268ece349321`:

- `node scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.mjs`
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check`
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check`
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --write` (to refresh the hash after `main` moved)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` (4 files, 538 tests)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` (1 file, 9 tests)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` (1 file, 280 tests)

The focused dispatch coverage now includes the durable `once` policy path and verifies suppressed plugin-binding route replies do not count as delivered before a later visible notice. The ACP projector truncation test asserts status-notice tagging, and the plugin SDK public surface budget is pinned to the current branch count.

target.title: fix(firecrawl,brave,web-search,web-fetch,models-config): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

All runtime config lookup paths use `"<key>" in <configObj>` to check whether a config field is present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited property (e.g. via `Object.create({provider: "malicious"})`) could be mistaken for an explicit user config entry and override the normal env/default path.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. Config objects are plain POJOs from JSON, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while closing the prototype-chain attack surface.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as user config entries across all runtime config lookup paths.

### Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-tools.test.ts src/web-search/runtime.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-tools.fetch.test.ts src/agents/models-config.merge.test.ts src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/ extensions/brave/` — all pass
- `git diff --check` — no whitespace issues

实时运行时证明：继承的属性被忽略，自身属性被保留
以下终端输出来自独立 Node.js 脚本，在 Node v16.17.1 环境中运行，模拟了 PR 修改的 5 处 in → Object.hasOwn() 变更的实际行为。


LIVE RUNTIME PROOF: inherited vs own config property checks

```
Node v16.17.1
─── Scenario 1: Prototype-inherited 'firecrawl' on search config ───
search object created via Object.create({ firecrawl: ... })
  search.firecrawl (direct access): PROTO-key
  'firecrawl' in search (OLD): true
  Object.hasOwn(search, 'firecrawl') (NEW): false

  OLD code (in operator) resolves firecrawl config to: apiKey=PROTO-key
  NEW code (Object.hasOwn) resolves firecrawl config to: undefined ✓ (CORRECT)

  ❌ OLD BEHAVIOR: Inherited proto property leaked into config resolution
  ✅ NEW BEHAVIOR: Inherited proto property correctly ignored

─── Scenario 2: Own 'firecrawl' property on search config ───
search object with own firecrawl property:
  'firecrawl' in searchWithOwn (OLD): true
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithOwn, 'firecrawl') (NEW): true

  OLD code resolves: apiKey=OWN-key
  NEW code resolves: apiKey=OWN-key

  ✅ Both old and new correctly find own property

─── Scenario 3: Inherited 'provider' on tools.web.search ───
web.search object with inherited 'provider':
  'provider' in search (OLD): true
  Object.hasOwn(search, 'provider') (NEW): false
  OLD resolves provider to: "brave"
  NEW resolves provider to: ""

  🎯 EXACT FIX: Old code would see proto-brave as user's chosen provider
     New code ignores it → provider falls through to runtime default/env

─── Scenario 4: Inherited 'contextWindow' in model config merge ───
explicitModel created via Object.create({ contextWindow: 99000 })
  'contextWindow' in explicitModel (OLD): true
  Object.hasOwn(explicitModel, 'contextWindow') (NEW): false
  OLD: explicitPresent=true → picks value=99000
  NEW: explicitPresent=false → falls through to implicit=128000

  ✅ OLD would override with proto-inherited 99000 instead of correct 128000
  ✅ NEW correctly ignores proto value, uses implicit model's 128000

### SUMMARY

The fix changes 6 files, replacing `'key' in obj` with `Object.hasOwn(obj, 'key')`:
  1. extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts       — firecrawl search/fetch config lookup
  2. extensions/brave/web-search-shared.ts     — brave legacy credential lookup
  3. src/web-search/runtime.ts                 — web search provider resolution
  4. src/web-fetch/runtime.ts                  — web fetch provider resolution
  5. src/agents/models-config.merge.ts         — model token/input override merge

Without this fix, any config object created via Object.create() with
prototype properties would leak inherited values into runtime decisions.
This is particularly relevant in config merging where the user wrote no
explicit value, but a prototype chain carries a stale or default value.

With Object.hasOwn(), only properties actually present on the object itself
(i.e., values the user explicitly configured) influence runtime behavior.

```
关键结论：

in 运算符会遍历原型链，把继承的属性误认为用户显式配置
Object.hasOwn() 只检查对象自身属性，原型链值不会泄漏到运行时决策中
自身属性不受影响（两种方式都能正确读取）
所有 5 处变更覆盖了 Firecrawl、Brave、Web Search、Web Fetch、Model Config Merge 中的配置读取路径

### Files Changed

| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts` | `"firecrawl" in search/fetch` → `Object.hasOwn()` (2) |
| `extensions/brave/web-search-shared.ts` | `"apiKey" in search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |
| `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts` | New: tests for own-property behavior |
| `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | `"provider" in search/params.search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (4) |
| `src/web-fetch/runtime.ts` | `"provider" in params.fetch` → `Object.hasOwn()` (2) |
| `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts` | `maxCharsCap/maxResponseBytes/provider/userAgent` → `Object.hasOwn()` (4) |
| `src/agents/models-config.merge.ts` | `contextWindow/contextTokens/maxTokens/input/reasoning` → `Object.hasOwn()` (5) |
| `src/cli/capability-cli.ts` | `"apiKey" in value` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts` | `"apiKey" in search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |

target.title: fix(sandbox): preserve active work during Docker config rollout
target.body:
Closes #103465
Follow-up: #103542
Filesystem operation-scope follow-up: #103611

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading an existing Docker sandbox could have an active command or browser operation interrupted when the container's config hash was stale. The old rollout guard inferred activity from a five-minute registry timestamp, so long-running work could be force-removed even though it was still running.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docker sandbox activity now uses one process-local per-container read/write lifecycle coordinator. Exec processes, filesystem bridge commands, and authenticated sandbox browser requests hold shared leases; automatic config rollout claims an exclusive mutation, drains active work, rechecks current container state, and only then replaces it. Explicit `openclaw sandbox recreate` remains an immediate operator action, and an unconfirmed process-wait failure hard-stops the child before releasing its lease.

The sandbox browser bridge now marks only authenticated pre-dispatch refresh responses. The registered loopback client retries those marked requests within the original timeout and abort budget, keeps the same control port while the backing container's mapped CDP port changes, and treats generic or non-loopback `503` responses as terminal. Hung-CDP cleanup queues behind active readers and rechecks the current container and auth token before removal.

## User Impact

Automatic Docker sandbox updates no longer kill active work. Once the real operation finishes, the queued replacement rechecks the container before applying current config. Browser requests that reach the authenticated refresh gate retry transparently across the stable bridge URL, while explicit recreation continues to stop selected runtimes immediately after confirmation.

## Evidence

- Deterministic regressions cover running stale-hash ordinary and browser containers with active leases; neither `rm` nor `create` runs before release.
- Original focused Testbox-through-Crabbox proof on `tbx_01kx5drxa4zj2q82ar4h8r5x6c`: 73 tests passed across process supervision, sandbox coordination/backend/config rollout, exec failure cleanup, and browser bridge auth/activity.
- Follow-up focused proof on `tbx_01kx5n426eevbmdbzkj8st6v1s`: 69 tests passed across sandbox activity/browser lifecycle, browser bridge auth/client retry behavior, and the plugin SDK bridge facade. Exact extension-test typecheck, touched core/extension lint, docs MDX, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Real Docker drain proof: an Alpine command remained running while graceful removal waited, then exited successfully and the container was removed (`{"during":"running","operationCode":0,"removed":true}`).
- Real Docker browser-rollout proof on `tbx_01kx5n426eevbmdbzkj8st6v1s`: an authenticated marked POST survived replacement of a real labeled browser container; the container ID changed, the bridge rebound to the identical URL, and the POST completed (`{"stableBridgeUrl":true,"containerReplaced":true,"markedPostRetried":true}`).
- `pnpm build`: passed on `tbx_01kx5n426eevbmdbzkj8st6v1s` after the final browser changes. The earlier exact branch build also passed on `tbx_01kx5g8qys4hcm17s9w7dq7w0y` ([Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29078035554)).
- The original exact diff passed `pnpm check:changed`. After the follow-up patch, all four typecheck lanes and the full core lint fan-out passed; final exact touched type/lint/format/docs lanes then passed after two test-only fixture cleanups.
- Fresh structured autoreview on the final local patch reported no findings: `patch is correct` (confidence `0.88`).

## Release Note Context

target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

macOS hatch and WebChat can make a slow first assistant reply look timed out or stuck when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side run budget. The gateway may have accepted the request and kept the assistant run active, but the macOS client did not consistently give every WebChat send path the same first-run-sized window or refresh history after terminal completion.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short gateway request/ACK deadline from the assistant run budget. `GatewayConnection.chatSend` keeps its request-sized default so unrelated callers such as Talk Mode retain their existing policy, while all three `MacGatewayChatTransport` paths—direct send, selected-agent/routing-contract send, and outbox route-lease replay—explicitly use a 300,000 ms WebChat run budget.

The shared chat view model now reads its pending/completion budget from the active transport. The shared default remains 120 seconds, macOS WebChat opts into five minutes, and the existing `agent.wait` gateway surface triggers a history refresh after a terminal result. The patch does not change gateway protocol shape, provider routing, authentication, model selection, channel delivery, schema, migrations, or session persistence.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant can keep seeing an accepted slow first reply as pending beyond 30 seconds instead of receiving a premature client timeout. Gateway connection failures still use the short request deadline, and a terminal assistant result refreshes history and clears the pending run through the shared chat state owner.

## Evidence

- Exact local head: `4ee0f49388c845823341eb8d84a9602783c0dce9`.
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --skip-update --filter GatewayConnectionControlTests` — 23 tests passed. Coverage includes request/run timeout separation, direct and targeted WebChat sends, outbox route-lease replay, `agent.wait` request encoding, and terminal-versus-active completion reconciliation.
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --skip-update --filter "completion wait"` — 3 tests passed. Coverage includes completion-triggered history refresh and pending clear, the shared 120-second default, and the transport-specific 300-second override.
- `corepack pnpm native:i18n:check` — passed with `entries=2916 changed=false`.
- Targeted SwiftFormat passed for the five touched Swift files outside `ChatViewModelTests.swift`. The all-changed-Swift lint reports eight diagnostics in untouched regions of `ChatViewModelTests.swift`; the same eight rules reproduce against `origin/main` at the corresponding baseline lines. `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passes.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos -c debug --product OpenClaw --build-path apps/macos/.build/arm64 --arch arm64 --skip-update -Xlinker -rpath -Xlinker @executable_path/../Frameworks` — passed on the current head after the latest-main chat view-model file split.
- Current-head live pending proof exercised `OpenClawChatViewModel` and `MacGatewayChatTransport` against a real local gateway. At 32.01 seconds, the gateway was healthy, the request ACK had returned (`is_sending=false`), the assistant run remained tracked (`pending_run_count=1`), and no client error was present. This proves the production path survives the former 30-second cutoff. The isolated bounded run was intentionally aborted after the observation and cleaned up.
- The bounded live run intentionally stopped after proving the former timeout boundary. Completion-triggered history refresh and pending clear are demonstrated by the current-head focused Swift tests above, not claimed as live completion proof.
- Visual composer proof was blocked because the macOS login window covered the app window; no screenshot or click-through proof is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users invoking the `computer` tool through gateway-visible tool surfaces could provide malformed numeric values and have them coerced into desktop actions instead of rejected when issuing scroll, hold-key, or wait actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The computer tool now uses the existing strict numeric readers at the execution boundary for `scrollAmount` and `duration`, matching the owner-local guard pattern used by adjacent node-control numeric inputs. ## User Impact

Malformed desktop-control numeric inputs now fail early with actionable validation errors, so invalid raw tool invocations cannot turn booleans, fractional scroll ticks, or nonnumeric durations into unintended computer-control actions.

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `ee16d404117`. Method: `directSessionReq` — same handler code path as WebSocket RPC (`sessionsHandlers["sessions.create"]`). All 7 scenarios pass on both `gateway-server` and `gateway-methods` test configurations.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 7-scenario response table in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed)
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

target.title: fix(skills): reject skill downloads exceeding 100 MB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`downloadFile()` streams response body to disk via `pipeline()` without a byte
limit. A hostile server can send unbounded data, exhausting disk space.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `SKILL_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (100 MiB) enforced via a Transform stream
counter inside the pipeline. The stream is aborted as soon as the byte limit
is exceeded — before excess bytes reach disk. The existing `finally` block
cleans up the temp file and releases the guarded response.

## User Impact

**Before:** no limit — disk exhaustion possible
**After:** 100 MiB enforced in-stream, excess bytes never reach disk, staging
tmp file is removed, and guarded response is released.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/install-download-maxbytes` | Base: `upstream/main` | Node: v22.19.0 — linux

### Real behavior proof

Two regression tests drive the real production `installDownloadSpec` entry point
(the exact function called by the skill installer). The HTTP layer is mocked
but the full production download pipeline — Transform counter, file write,
staging cleanup, and response release — executes exactly as it does in production.

**Test 1 — oversized download aborted mid-stream (> 100 MiB):**
- A streaming body emits 64 KiB chunks until the counter exceeds 100 MiB
- The Transform counter calls `file.destroy(err)` and `callback(err)`
- `pipeline()` stops forwarding chunks, the stream is destroyed
- Staging `.tmp` file is cleaned up by the `finally` block
- Guarded `release()` is called

**Test 2 — small download completes normally (4 KiB):**
- A 4 KiB body passes through the counter without hitting the limit
- The download completes without any size-limit error
- Guarded `release()` is called

target.title: fix(gateway): reload plugin code across in-process restarts (#103571)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An in-process gateway restart (SIGUSR1 / `gateway restart --safe` under `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`) re-runs each plugin's `register()` and logs `<plugin> registered` — but serves the module graph cached from the original process start. Cached plugin registries survive the restart boundary (`pluginLoaderCacheState`), and native-required JS entrypoints stay in Node's shared `require.cache`, so updated **workspace plugin code** on disk (e.g. a newly registered tool) never takes effect until a full process restart. Config changes *do* reload because the restart iteration hook already calls `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` — plugin caches were the missing symmetric clear. Fixes #103571.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart is the repo's documented **explicit reload boundary** for process-stable plugin state ("Plugin metadata changes require restart or explicit plugin owner reload/install/doctor flow" — `src/plugins/AGENTS.md`). Add `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` in the plugins loader (drops cached registries + activated runtime state, manifest read caches, and purges previously imported plugin entrypoints from `require.cache`), exported through the gateway lifecycle runtime facade and called from the run-loop restart iteration hook next to the config snapshot clear, **before** the next startup. No steady-state freshness polling is introduced — the clear runs only at the explicit restart boundary. No new options or public API surface.

## User Impact

Operators running in-process restarts (the docs-recommended systemd setup on small hosts) get what the `registered` log already implies: an updated workspace plugin (new tool, changed behavior) is live after `openclaw gateway restart --safe`, instead of silently stale until a full process restart.

## Evidence

Two tests, both discriminating:
- `run-loop.test.ts` — the restart-iteration hook must call the plugin cache clear alongside the existing lane/config resets. **Fails on main** (`clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart` never called: `1 failed | 40 passed`), passes with this PR (41/41).
- `loader.restart-reload.test.ts` (new) — real temp workspace plugin registering `probe_tool_v1` → source+manifest edited on disk to `probe_tool_v2` → reload **without** the clear still serves v1 (reproduces the reported staleness) → reload **after** `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` loads `probe_tool_v2` from disk.

target.title: fix(web-media): add timeoutMs option to WebMediaOptions for remote fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadWebMedia` / `loadWebMediaRaw` accepted `readIdleTimeoutMs` (idle timeout between data chunks) but had no overall request timeout for remote HTTP fetches. A server that accepts the connection then never sends headers — or withholds response data — held the download open indefinitely. The Tlon download/upload fetch paths had the same gap: only a body-idle guard, no total deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the **canonical** PR for the shared `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs` seam plus the Tlon caller wiring. It exposes the existing `readRemoteMediaBuffer` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs` (an `AbortSignal`-backed total request lifetime) through `loadWebMediaInternal`, and applies it at the two Tlon remote-fetch call sites.

The total deadline is `15 * 60_000` (15 min), **aligning with the canonical bounded-media ceiling** established by the merged node-camera fix (#103266, `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`). A shorter cap was flagged by ClawSweeper as a P1 compatibility risk because `timeoutMs` stays active through complete body consumption and would newly fail slow-but-progressing transfers; 15 min matches the accepted precedent while `readIdleTimeoutMs` (30 s for Tlon) continues to bound body-idle stalls on a tighter schedule.

Sibling caller PRs (telegram #103020, qqbot #103018, agent-tools #103209) apply the same invariant at distinct caller boundaries; the Tlon-only #103199 is closed as a subset of this PR.

## User Impact

- Remote media fetches that previously hung forever on a never-responding endpoint now abort after the total deadline and reach their established fallback: `downloadMedia` → `null`, `uploadImageFromUrl` → original URL.
- Slow-but-progressing transfers are unaffected: they remain bounded by `readIdleTimeoutMs`, and 15 min is the accepted ceiling for legitimate large transfers.
- Callers of `loadWebMedia`/`loadWebMediaRaw` can now opt into `timeoutMs` to cap total request duration.

## Evidence

**Source:**
- `src/media/web-media.ts`: added `timeoutMs?: number` to `WebMediaOptions`; forwarded through `loadWebMediaInternal` into the `readRemoteMediaBuffer` call.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts`: `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` / `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`, passed into the shared fetch options; existing null / original-URL fallback paths unchanged.

**Tests (focused suite, run locally via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`; Crabbox unavailable in this environment so the allowed local fallback was used):**
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts` / `upload.test.ts`: switched the two exact-match `toHaveBeenCalledWith` assertions to `expect.objectContaining(...)` and assert `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000`; retained the `returns null` / `returns original URL` fallback coverage.
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts`: added `aborts a stalled remote fetch via the overall timeoutMs deadline` — a controlled stalled-endpoint test where the fetch accepts the connection but never returns headers; the guarded-fetch abort signal fires at the `timeoutMs` deadline and `loadWebMediaRaw` rejects.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where qmd-backed memory search could report invalid JSON when qmd writes bracketed log lines such as `[INFO]` before the actual result array.

## Why This Change Was Made

The noisy stdout parser now scans complete top-level qmd result arrays in one pass, skips bracketed log prefixes and malformed bracket fragments, and preserves nested JSON inside valid qmd results. The change stays inside the memory-host qmd parser and adds focused parser and memory-core manager coverage for the noisy stdout path.

## User Impact

Memory search can tolerate common qmd/native stdout prefixes and still return matching results instead of failing the lookup. Malformed log fragments before the result array no longer amplify parsing into repeated suffix scans.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: qmd stdout with bracketed log prefixes or malformed bracket fragments before the result array is skipped, while nested arrays inside valid qmd result objects are preserved until the enclosing top-level result array is parsed.

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup needed a guided path that proves a usable receive transport before users rely on the channel, without OpenClaw creating or managing a Signal Docker container. Existing setup and status paths could also leave stale native/container transport fields ambiguous, miss account-specific API-mode behavior, or report a Signal daemon as generically working when the configured account was missing or receive was unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal plugin now owns a setup wizard path for two supported transports: local `signal-cli` and an existing Signal server managed by the operator. The same change tightens native/container/auto probing so setup and status can distinguish transport reachability from account/receive readiness, and it lets multi-account Signal configs use `channels.signal.apiMode` as a channel default with per-account overrides.

## User Impact

Users can run Signal setup, choose local `signal-cli` or an existing server URL, and have setup save config only after the selected transport is reachable for the intended account. Operators get clearer `openclaw channels status --probe` and health output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states. Existing/manual `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api` deployments remain supported through `apiMode: "container"`; OpenClaw no longer offers an OpenClaw-managed Signal Docker setup path.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Existing-server setup prompts for a Signal account, probes the server with that account, and saves `httpUrl`, `autoStart: false`, and `apiMode: "auto"` after the probe succeeds.
- Native setup clears stale external/container endpoint fields for the intended account while preserving existing custom native endpoints and channel-level `channels.signal.apiMode` defaults.
- Container receive readiness is checked through `/v1/receive/{account}` when receive capability is required, and container account validation uses bounded `/v1/accounts` reads.
- Signal send, reaction, monitor, attachment, and probe paths resolve account-specific `apiMode` before falling back to the channel default.
- `openclaw channels status --probe` and health formatting expose Signal readiness states instead of reducing account-missing/receive-unavailable cases to a generic “works” signal.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard, gateway status, config, docs, and tests rather than browser UI; command output is the reviewer-checkable proof.

target.title: fix(plugins): enhance plugin API compatibility diagnostic messages with troubleshooting guidance
target.body:
## Summary

Plugin API compatibility discovery-skip warnings now include actionable troubleshooting guidance so users can self-diagnose version mismatches instead of seeing a bare error.

- **Problem**: When plugin discovery is skipped due to plugin API version mismatch (e.g., "host is 2026.5.28" on a 2026.6.8 install), the warning message provides no guidance on how to diagnose or resolve the mismatch.
- **Solution**: Extend the two `shouldSkipIncompatiblePackagePluginApi` diagnostic messages with hints pointing to `openclaw --version`, `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION`, and `openclaw doctor`.
- **What changed**: `src/plugins/discovery.ts` — 2 diagnostic messages enhanced (2 lines)
- **What did NOT change**: No runtime behavior, no version resolution, no discovery logic, no config schema, no other plugin metadata paths
- **Relationship to #95384**: This PR is a **complementary UX improvement** — it adds diagnostic troubleshooting hints. PR #95384 fixes the root cause (stale host-version propagation during update). They address different layers of the same issue and do not conflict.
- **Relationship to #94560**: Also complementary — #94560 handles the RPC finalizer child path for stale env vars; this PR improves the user-facing diagnostic text when discovery is skipped.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #93908
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #93908 reports a Feishu plugin discovery failure where the gateway skips the plugin with the message "plugin requires plugin API >=2026.6.8, but this host is 2026.5.28; skipping discovery" despite a 2026.6.8 install. The reporter has no idea what to check next — the message states the problem but offers no path to resolution. Meanwhile, the install path (`src/plugins/install.ts:207-213`) already includes troubleshooting hints like "Upgrade OpenClaw and retry" and "set OPENCLAW_VERSION and retry." This PR brings the discovery-skip diagnostics to the same standard.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Plugin discovery-skip warnings for API version mismatches and invalid metadata now include actionable troubleshooting guidance.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux (x64), Node v24, branch `fix/feishu-plugin-api-diag-93908` at commit `9672ced539b`
- **Real discovery output after this patch**:

```console
$ npx tsx scripts/repro-diag-messages.mjs

[WARN] /tmp/.../extensions/future-plugin/package.json
  Message: plugin requires plugin API >=2099.1.0, but this host is 2026.6.11;
           skipping discovery (check "openclaw --version",
           OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION, or run "openclaw doctor")

[WARN] /tmp/.../extensions/malformed-plugin/package.json
  Message: invalid package plugin API metadata: package.json
           openclaw.compat.pluginApi must be a string; skipping discovery
           (check package.json openclaw.compat.pluginApi)

=== Verification ===
Version mismatch hint present: ✅ YES
Invalid metadata hint present: ✅ YES
```

- **Exact steps to reproduce**:
  1. Create a plugin dir with `compat.pluginApi: ">=2099.1.0"` (future version)
  2. Create a plugin dir with malformed `compat.pluginApi: 12345` (non-string)
  3. Run `discoverOpenClawPlugins({ env })`
  4. Observe enhanced diagnostic messages with troubleshooting hints

- **Existing test suite**: 76/76 discovery tests pass, including `messageIncludes` assertions that confirm backward compatibility

**Before/After comparison**:

| Diagnostic | Before | After |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Invalid metadata | `invalid package plugin API metadata: …; skipping discovery` | `… (check package.json openclaw.compat.pluginApi)` |
| Version mismatch | `plugin requires plugin API >=X, but this host is Y; skipping discovery` | `… (check "openclaw --version", OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION, or run "openclaw doctor")` |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 76 discovery tests pass with `messageIncludes` matching — the added text does not break existing assertions
  2. The invalid-metadata diagnostic now points users to the specific `package.json` field to check
  3. The version-mismatch diagnostic now provides 3 actionable next steps: verify gateway version, check env vars, run doctor
  4. Real discovery execution confirms enhanced messages appear in actual diagnostic output
  5. Message format aligns with the existing pattern in `src/plugins/install.ts:207-213` which already includes troubleshooting guidance
- **What was not tested**:
  1. Live Windows npm-global install with Feishu plugin (requires Windows environment)
  2. Actual `openclaw doctor` flow end-to-end with stale version metadata
  3. Gateway startup with `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION` override on Windows

## Root Cause

N/A — this is a diagnostic UX improvement. The underlying version mismatch in #93908 is most likely environmental (stale npm install, PATH issues, or `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION` / `npm_package_version` env-var leakage). The message now equips users to self-diagnose.

## Regression Test Plan

N/A — existing `src/plugins/discovery.test.ts` tests (76 passing) already cover the message content via `messageIncludes` assertions. The enhanced messages are backward-compatible with these assertions.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users who encounter a plugin API compatibility discovery-skip will now see diagnostic messages with troubleshooting hints:

- `… skipping discovery (check package.json openclaw.compat.pluginApi)`
- `… skipping discovery (check "openclaw --version", OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION, or run "openclaw doctor")`

No other user-visible changes.

- **Complementary to #95384**: #95384 fixes the root cause (stale version propagation during update); this PR improves the user-facing diagnostic when discovery is skipped for any reason. Both are independently valuable.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord reasoning messages that wrap content in `_…_` would corrupt markdown code fences and inline code when the message was split across chunks. After a chunk boundary that started with a code delimiter, the italics rebalancer could prepend `_` (breaking `_```python` / `_~~~` / `_`code``) or leave unmatched trailing `_` on continuation chunks.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rebalanceReasoningItalics` still closes/reopens reasoning italics so each Discord message stays independently balanced. When the next chunk starts with a code delimiter:

1. Do **not** prepend `_` onto the code opener.
2. Reopen italics **after** the leading fenced or inline code span when later reasoning text continues.
3. Drop a lone trailing `_` on pure-code continuations.
4. Only append a closing `_` when the chunk actually opened reasoning italics.

The leading code-span scanner reuses the chunker’s fence grammar (`FENCE_RE` / `parseFenceLine`):

- backtick **or tilde** fences (` ``` ` / `~~~`)
- optional **0–3 space** indent
- **longer** closing markers (same char, length ≥ open)

Regression tests assert exact second-chunk output and even `_` counts for backtick, tilde, indented, longer-close, inline, and pure-code cases.

## User Impact

Discord reasoning/thinking replies that contain code blocks or inline code no longer break markdown fences at chunk boundaries, including tilde and indented fences, and each chunk keeps balanced reasoning italics when text continues after code.

## Evidence

### Focused tests
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

### Production-path harness (`chunkDiscordText` → `rebalanceReasoningItalics`)

**Current main (before):** second chunk could start with `_```python…` (broken fence).

**This patch (exact second chunks):**
```
tilde:      "~~~python\nprint(1)\n~~~\n_more_"
indent:     "  ```python\nprint(1)\n  ```\n_more_"
long-close: "```python\nprint(1)\n````\n_more_"
```
All chunks have even `_` counts; openers are not prefixed with `_`.

### Changed-lane gates
```
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs  # PASS
pnpm test:changed  # PASS (extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts, 24 tests)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Discord reasoning-italics rebalance protects code-leading openers using the full chunker fence grammar and keeps per-message `_` balance.
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout, Node 24; production helper `chunkDiscordText`. Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).
- Current-main contrast: with `maxLines: 10`, a reasoning body whose continuation starts at a fenced block produced `_```…` on main; incomplete parsers also missed tilde / indented / longer-close forms.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node --import tsx` harness for tilde, indented, and longer-close fixtures
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts`
  3. `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`
  4. `pnpm test:changed`
- Evidence after fix: exact second-chunk outputs above; 24/24 tests green including tilde, indented, longer-close, inline, and pure-code cases.
- Control check: normal multi-chunk reasoning still reopens with leading `_` on non-code continuations.
- Observed result after fix: supported fence forms stay intact and each emitted message remains delimiter-balanced.
- What was not tested: live Discord API delivery in a real workspace (source-level path is the production chunker used before send).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation, tests, and proof were verified against ClawSweeper review findings on #103166 (balance code-leading chunks; reuse full fence grammar).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers using an explicit gateway client readiness timeout could pass an oversized finite value that reached the readiness waiter without the safe timer clamp used by the default timeout path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The explicit timeout path now reuses the existing finite timeout delay resolver with the same zero-minimum boundary before starting the client. This keeps the gateway-client readiness boundary local and avoids adding new config, fallback behavior, or broader policy.

## User Impact

Developers can pass explicit readiness timeouts without accidentally forwarding timer values above the safe Node.js delay range to alternate readiness waiters.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: explicit gateway-client readiness timeouts are clamped to `MAX_SAFE_TIMEOUT_DELAY_MS` before the exported startup helper invokes an alternate readiness waiter, and startup still proceeds after readiness succeeds.

target.title: fix(slack): remember resolved channel types so mpDM bot messages key one session (#102676)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Slack multi-party DM (`mpim`) room produces **two parallel sessions per agent**. Human-authored messages carry `channel_type: "mpim"` on the event and key `slack:group:<channelId>`; bot-authored inbound shapes omit `channel_type`, and when the `conversations.info` fill cannot resolve the type either, C-prefix inference falls back to `"channel"` and keys a second `slack:channel:<channelId>` session for the same room. Modern mpDM ids are C-prefixed, so prefix inference cannot disambiguate. (Fixes #102676.)

## Why This Change Was Made

The room's type is **already known** from events previously seen for it — the fix carries that knowledge forward instead of rediscovering (or guessing). An `observedType` field on the existing `channelCache` entry remembers explicit `channel_type` values after `normalizeSlackChannelType` resolves them; the resolution chain becomes `event type → channel-info fill → remembered type → prefix inference`. The system-event authorization path (`authorizeSlackSystemEventSender`) consults the same memory so `message_changed` / `message_deleted` events key identically, and remembers the type on success for future events.

Relative to closed attempts on this issue: **no new network lookups** (#102752 added one and was closed for it), and it fixes the reported **C-prefixed** path mechanism itself rather than special-casing an ID prefix (#102702 only changed G-prefixed IDs). The remembered value is a *last* fallback — an explicit event type or successful `conversations.info` result always wins.

## User Impact

One session per agent per mpDM room: agents keep a single conversation context and history instead of silently splitting across `slack:group:` and `slack:channel:` keys when bots talk to each other. No config change; no new public options; no behavior change for public/private channels (`slack:channel:`), DMs (`slack:direct:`), or G-prefixed group DMs.

## ClawSweeper Review Fixes Applied

Fixes from ClawSweeper review:

1. **Merged `channelTypeMemory` into `channelCache`** — replaced the separate Map with an `observedType` field on the existing `ChannelCacheEntry`, eliminating a second classification owner that could drift.

2. **Fixed system-event authorization path** — `authorizeSlackSystemEventSender` now calls `recallSlackChannelType` in its type-resolution chain (before C-prefix inference fallback), and remembers the resolved type on authorization success. Also added `eventScope` pass-through for Enterprise Grid compatibility.

3. **Added system-event regression tests** — `context.test.ts` now covers `resolveSlackSystemEventSessionKey` with primed and unprimed recall.

## Files Changed

- **extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts** — Add `observedType` to `ChannelCacheEntry`; `rememberSlackChannelType`/`recallSlackChannelType` now read/write channelCache instead of a separate Map; recall fallback in `resolveSlackSystemEventSessionKey`
- **extensions/slack/src/monitor/auth.ts** — Add `eventScope` param, `recallSlackChannelType` fallback in type-resolution chain; remember resolved type on auth success
- **extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/system-event-context.ts** — Add `eventScope` param pass-through
- **extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts** — Add recall fallback in `resolveSlackConversationContext` type-resolution chain; remember resolved type after every message
- **extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.test.ts** — Regression test for human+bot same-mpDM classification; add new methods to mock context
- **extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.test.ts** — System-event recall regression tests (primed + unprimed paths)

target.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users interacting with agents through external chats such as WhatsApp could see automatic runtime notices when model fallback, usage limits, compaction, backend failures, heartbeat checks, ACP status, plugin-binding failures, or tool/progress warnings happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `messages.operationalReplies` so operators can control automatic operational notices separately from normal assistant replies. The policy supports `always`, `silent`, `once`, and `redirect`; `redirect` writes notices to an operator session through `redirectSessionKey`, and `sendPolicy: deny` still wins.

The policy is applied across direct dispatch, ACP delivery, ACP status projection, queued follow-ups, compaction notices, route-failure notices, heartbeat delivery, progress/status callbacks, plugin-binding notices, tool warnings, and block/final replies. Normal message-tool replies, authorized command replies, before-run block replies, and background ACP child suppression keep their existing behavior.

The branch was rebased during follow-up, and the unrelated WhatsApp shrinkwrap delta was removed from the PR. The `once` policy now records delivered notice fingerprints on the source session, so duplicate suppression survives process restarts instead of relying only on an in-memory set.

## User Impact

Operators can keep fallback, usage-limit, backend-error, compaction, heartbeat, status, ACP, follow-up, plugin-binding, and tool-warning notices out of external chats while still preserving logs or redirecting those notices to an operator-owned session. Existing configs keep current behavior because the default policy is `always`.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof: WhatsApp-like Source Chat

Earlier redacted terminal proof on this branch used the actual `applyOperationalReplyPolicy` helper, a real temp `sessions.json`, and a source context shaped like an external WhatsApp direct chat:

- source channel: `whatsapp`
- source session: `agent:main:whatsapp:direct:redacted-user`
- payload: `isError: true`, `isFallbackNotice: true`, text `model fallback failed; usage limit reached`

Observed output:

```text
silent: shouldDeliverToSourceChat=false, intentionalSilence=true, externalSends=0, opsTranscriptBytes=0
redirect: shouldDeliverToSourceChat=false, redirected=true, externalSends=0, opsTranscriptHasSourceSession=true, opsTranscriptHasSourceChannel=true, opsTranscriptHasNoticeText=true
redirect transcript excerpt: sourceSessionKey: agent:main:whatsapp:direct:redacted-user | sourceChannel: whatsapp | kind: error
```

This proves the affected external-source path does not deliver the operational fallback/error notice back to the source chat under `silent`, and under `redirect` it keeps source chat sends at zero while writing the notice, source session, source channel, and notice kind into the configured operator session transcript.

### Local Validation

Latest follow-up validation after rebasing on current `origin/main` and pushing `0c11afd128c71cd22d29cf9e7881268ece349321`:

- `node scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.mjs`
